correctedAssumptionsRead: Steady current in a thin-wire one-dimensional approximation, with constant carrier number density and resistivity.
Material, length, cross-section, temperature and supply conditions are held fixed.
Significant curvature effects and contact-region current redistribution are excluded.
The unchanged quantities are approximate cross-sectional averages within the model, not exactly equal local fields throughout any real bend.
Figure 169 explicitly illustrates the model's internal longitudinal/tangential field, not a universal claim about arbitrarily sharp bends.
remainingFullTextRead: Internal normal-field components drive charge redistribution until steady state.
External fields may have a normal component while retaining a longitudinal component.
The castor-oil and wet-wood experiment concerns observing field directions; no apparatus is supplied by figure 169.
Source terminal charges, distributed surface charges and finite-speed field establishment are discussed after the figure.
A steady surface charge density can coexist with moving charge, and the steady field is described by a potential.

mathematicalEvidence: The two boundary bends and three nested field bends share center [185,311]. Their radii are 115, 100.75, 86.5, 72.25 and 58, so each field track is strictly between the two boundaries.
Each bend endpoint is the endpoint of its corresponding vertical arm. The circle radius at these joins is horizontal, making the arc tangent vertical like the arm.
The six internal arrow displacements have zero horizontal component; left vertical displacements are positive and right displacements negative in mathematical y-up space.
Each of the four opening curves joins x127 to x243, has a rightward arrow, and retains the descending source arch prominence/order.
Each exterior branch is separately represented, with circle endpoint/arrow-on-curve assertions, nonzero horizontal/vertical displacement and the source-directed arrow.
No internal field curve crosses another field curve or a conductor boundary in any opened preview.
physicalAndMathematicalFidelity.modelInterpretation: Qualitative field-direction diagram of the corrected thin-wire approximation. Equal-looking track spacing, exact circular construction and the drawn bend do not assert exact local electric-field magnitude in a real curved conductor. Exterior oblique fields do not contradict the internal tangential boundary condition.
